rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The common reading has “mosques” in the plural; Mujahid reads “the mosque” in the singular.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد المسجد على الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʿtikāf comes from staying; its basic sense is to remain somewhere continuously.
rows.anchor: الاعتكاف: العكوف، أصله اللزوم يقال: عكفت بالمكان إذا أقمت به ملازما له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Legally, iʿtikāf is confining oneself in a mosque for worship with intent and avoiding what invalidates it; the term retains its lexical sense.
rows.anchor: والاعتكاف: هو حبس النفس في المسجد على عبادة الله تعالى بشرط العزم، وترك ما يبطله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root sense of ḥadd is prevention; limits are so named because they prevent prohibited conduct that incurs a penalty.
rows.anchor: والحد: أصله المنع، ومنه سمي البواب حدادا، ومنه الإحداد، وحد الدار والحدود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومقاتل وغيرهم
rows.claim: The verse reportedly followed Companions in retreat leaving the mosque to have intercourse with their wives when a need arose, then washing and returning; they were forbidden to do so.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس وقتادة ومقاتل وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After explaining when intercourse is forbidden during fasting, God explains its prohibition during iʿtikāf so the rules are not mistaken for one another.
rows.anchor: لما بين تعالى وقت تحريم المباشرة في الصوم أتبعه ببيان تحريمها في الاعتكاف كيلا يظن أن التحريم فيهما سواء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك والحسن وقتادة وغيرهم
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes “approach them” to mean sexual intercourse.
rows.anchor: المراد به الجماع، عن ابن عباس والضحاك والحسن وقتادة وغيرهم

rows.speaker: ابن زيد ومالك بن أنس
rows.claim: A broader interpretation includes intercourse and lesser intimacies such as kissing.
rows.anchor: الجماع وكل ما دونه من قبلة ونحوها، عن ابن زيد ومالك بن أنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase describes people remaining in the mosque in retreat; iʿtikāf was familiar, so it is named without introduction and specified as taking place in mosques.
rows.anchor: أي ملازمون للمسجد معتكفا، والاعتكاف عبادة كانت معروفة عندهم، قلذلك أطلق، وبين اختصاصه بالمساجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Of the views that intercourse is prohibited because of iʿtikāf or because of the mosque, Jishumi prefers the first: it is unlawful even outside the mosque when one leaves for a need.
rows.anchor: والأول الوجه؛ لأنه لا يحل خارج المسجد إذا خرج لحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those” refers to the preceding rules for fasting, iʿtikāf, and related matters.
rows.anchor: تلك يعني الأحكام التي تقدمت في الصوم والاعتكاف وغيرها

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi explains God's limits as prescribed conditions.
rows.anchor: شروطه، عن السدي

rows.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
rows.claim: Shahr ibn Hawshab explains God's limits as obligations.
rows.anchor: فرائضه، عن شهر بن حوشب

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak explains God's limits as sins against God.
rows.anchor: معاصي الله، عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains God's limits as whatever God has forbidden.
rows.anchor: ما منع الله منه، عن الزجاج

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan explains God's limits as God's sanctities, echoing 22:30.
rows.anchor: حرمات الله، عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes God's limits as the boundaries separating what is forbidden from what is lawful.
rows.anchor: حدوده الفاصلة بين الحرام والحلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One gloss paraphrases “do not approach them” as “do not commit them.”
rows.anchor: قيل: فلا تأتوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss means not to approach God's limits by disobeying them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا تقربوها بالمخالفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's signs here are His proofs made clear to people.
rows.anchor: كذلك يبين الله آياته حججه للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose is that people avoid sins and adhere to obedience, through which godfearingness is attained.
rows.anchor: لكي يتقوا المعاصي، ويتمسكوا بالطاعات؛ لأن بها يتم التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A narrower gloss says the purpose is to avoid intercourse during iʿtikāf.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لتتقوا الجماع في الاعتكاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding discussion shows that ambiguous expressions suggesting improper meanings should not be applied to God or His Messenger in discussing divine names and attributes.
rows.anchor: في أسماء الله وصفاته قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawaddu means to love or want, from wudd, love; it can denote human will or a desire only God can fulfill.
rows.anchor: يود: يحب، وهو من الود، وهو المحبة، وهو يرجع إلى الإرادة التي هي فعل العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayr means the opposite of evil.
rows.anchor: والخير: نقيض الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To single something out is to be exclusive in it or to favor someone with it.
rows.anchor: والاختصاص بالشيء: هو الانفراد به، يقال: خصه بالشيء إذا فضله به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy is a benefit bestowed on someone in need.
rows.anchor: والرحمة: النعمة على المحتاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mushrikīn may be genitive as a coordinate of “People of the Book.”
rows.anchor: هو عطف على (أهل الكتاب)، فيكون مجرورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may instead be nominative as a coordinate of “those who disbelieved,” functioning as the subject.
rows.anchor: على (الذين كفروا)، وموضعه رفع؛ لأنه كالفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first min, in “People of the Book,” marks a category, as in “the impurity of idols.”
rows.anchor: الأولى من أهل الكتاب فهي للتنويع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The min before “good” is extra for emphasis, with the governed phrase in the nominative.
rows.anchor: والثانية التي مع خير فهي زائدة مؤكدة، كقولك: ما أتاني من أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The min in “from your Lord” marks the point of origin.
rows.anchor: والثالثة في من ربكم فلابتداء الغاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reportedly came when Muslims urged Jews to believe in Muhammad and his revelation; they replied that it was no better than their religion, though they wished it were good, and the verse exposed their claim.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية تكذيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book may mean Jews specifically or Jews and Christians together.
rows.anchor: قيل: أراد اليهود، ويحتمل اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists meant are the Arab polytheists.
rows.anchor: يعني مشركي العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Sent down upon you” may mean Muhammad and his Companions, or Muhammad alone with the plural used honorifically.
rows.anchor: يعني محمدا وأصحابه، وقيل: أراد محمدا، وكنى عنه بلفظ الجمع تعظيما

rows.speaker: الحسن وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and others take the good sent from God to be revelation.
rows.anchor: الوحي المنزل، عن الحسن وغيره

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm takes it to be the Book and wisdom.
rows.anchor: الكتاب والحكمة، عن الأصم

rows.speaker: الحسن وجماعة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and a group identify God's favor as prophethood.
rows.anchor: بالنبوة، عن الحسن وجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations identify the favor as reward or divine لطف; the latter does not mean God withholds لطف but gives it to those suited to benefit.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الإنعام بالثواب، وقيل: بالألطاف، وليس ذلك على أنه يمنع أحدا ألطافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says God chooses the most fitting recipient for His message rather than following people's wishes and demands.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يختص برسالته للأصلح، ولا يقف على شهوات الخلق واقتراحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every religious and worldly blessing originates with God without prior entitlement, showing the greatness of His bounty.
rows.anchor: فمنه تعالى ابتداء خلقه به من غير استحقاق سلف، فهو عظيم النعم والفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The usual reading has two nūns in atuhājjūnanā.
rows.anchor: القراءة الظاهرة (أتحاجوننا) بنونين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some readers use one nūn.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم بنون واحدة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj allows clear pronunciation, assimilation, or deletion.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: ويجوز فيه ثلاثة أوجه: الإظهار، والإدغام، والحذف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Argument, disputation, and quarrel are near-synonyms; muḥājjah is the reciprocal form of argument.
rows.anchor: الحجاج والجدال والخصام نظائر، والمحاجة مفاعلة من الحجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sincerity, singleness, and exclusivity are near-synonyms; the opposite of purity is admixture.
rows.anchor: والإخلاص والإفراد والاختصاص نظائر، ونقيض الخالص الشائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Work and action are near-synonyms; an action is something brought about by an agent.
rows.anchor: والعمل والفعل نظائر، والفعل: ما حدث عن قادر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative alif is used as a rebuke, though this construction may also indicate affirmation or confirmation.
rows.anchor: الألف في أتحاجوننا استفهام والمراد الإنكار، وقد يجيء ذلك بمعنى الإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reportedly followed the Jews' claim that prophets belonged to them and their religion, and that a true prophet would have come from them rather than the Arabs.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse answers the group's faulty argument and addresses Muhammad as he speaks to the Jews and others.
rows.anchor: ثم بين تعالى ما يبطل شبه القوم فقال تعالى: قل يا محمد لهؤلاء اليهود وغيرهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the question as “Are you disputing with us?”
rows.anchor: أتجادلوننا، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
rows.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd gloss it as “Are you quarrelling with us?”
rows.anchor: أتخاصموننا، عن مجاهد وابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says the Jews claimed greater entitlement to truth and prophethood because prophecy had appeared among them earlier.
rows.anchor: إنهم أولى بالحق والنبوة لتقدم النبوة فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says they claimed greater entitlement to faith than the Arabs who worshipped idols.
rows.anchor: نحن أحق بالإيمان من العرب الذين عبدوا الأوثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further account identifies their argument with the claim, “We are God's sons and beloved.”
rows.anchor: هي قوله (نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf is governed by jaʿalnā, with the force of saying God guided whom He willed and bestowed the favor of making this a middle community.
rows.anchor: والعامل في الكاف جعلنا تقديره: نهدي من نشاء، وقد أنعمنا عليهم بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although jaʿalnā conveys that God bestowed a favor, its wording specifically says “made.”
rows.anchor: إلا أن (جعلنا) يدل على أنعمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jewish leaders Marhab, al-Rabiʿ, and others told Muʿadh Muhammad changed the qibla from envy and their qibla was that of the prophets; Muʿadh replied Muslims followed justice and truth, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والربيع
rows.claim: After the qibla changed, people asked what would happen to prayers they had performed facing the former direction.
rows.anchor: كيف بأعمالنا التي كنا نعمل في قبلتنا الأولى؟، عن ابن عباس وقتادة والربيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says people asked about fellow Muslims who died before the change, including Saʿd ibn Zurārah and al-Barāʾ ibn Maʿrūr.
rows.anchor: وكان مات سعد بن زرارة والبراء بن معرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jishumi rejects that the Companions doubted their prayers; they may have wondered what their dead brothers would have done, which practice was better, or a hypocrite may have asked and God answered the believers.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون الصحابة شكت في صلاتهم حتى سألوا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Thus” must connect to what precedes; of the prior explanations, Jishumi prefers the one attributed to Abu al-Qasim.
rows.anchor: ولا بد من تعلق له بما تقدم، وقد ذكرنا ما قيل فيه، والأقرب ما قاله أبو القاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says God made the community middle through a لطف He knew would lead them all to agree on what is right.
rows.anchor: باللطف الذي هو علم الله تعالى أنه متى فعل بهم أجمعوا على الصواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes “made you” to mean God judged the community to be so or described it as such.
rows.anchor: وقيل: حكمنا لكم بذلك، ووصفناكم به أمة جماعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد والربيع
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, Mujahid, and al-Rabiʿ interpret “middle” as just; this is also reported from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قيل: عدلا، عن ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد والربيع، وروي مرفوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss takes “middle” to mean the best community.
rows.anchor: وقيل: خيارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view makes Muslims balanced between religious excess and neglect, following moderation and deserving reward.
rows.anchor: وسطا بين الغالي في الأديان وبين المقصر، فيجعل لهم القصد والثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concise wording implies that the community is right in all its affairs.
rows.anchor: وفيه مع إيجاز اللفظ دليل أنهم في جميع أمورهم على الصواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says Muslims are the just middle between Christians, excessive about Jesus, and Jews, who fell short.
rows.anchor: لما غلت النصارى في المسيح، وقصر اليهود كان قول المسلمين أوسطهم وأعدلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jishumi asks how the whole community can be described this way if some members lack the quality.
rows.anchor: ويقال: إذا كان في الأمة من ليس هذه صفته. فكيف وصفوا بذلك؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows punishment is deserved through deeds and warns against adopting their deterministic account of human action.
rows.anchor: سلوك طريقتهم في القول في الجبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has muṣaddiq in the nominative as an adjective modifying “Book.”
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة مصدق بالرفع على أنه نعت للكتاب

rows.speaker: إبراهيم عن أبي العالية
rows.claim: Ibrahim reports that Abu al-Aliyah read muṣaddiq in the accusative as a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: وعن إبراهيم عن أبي العالية مصدقا بالنصب على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kitāb means a written thing, that is, what has been written.
rows.anchor: الكتاب: الذي يكتب، وهو بمعنى المكتوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istiftāḥ means seeking victory; fatḥ means victory, opening something, or making its meaning clear.
rows.anchor: والاستفتاح: طلب الفتح، وهو طلب النصر (إن تستفتحوا فقد جاءكم الفتح)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basic sense of fatḥ is the opposite of closing.
rows.anchor: وأصل الفتح ضد الإغلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāna governs a nominative subject and an accusative predicate.
rows.anchor: كان فعل يرفع الاسم وينصب الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lexical verb denotes the coming into existence of its verbal meaning at a time, whereas kāna marks tense through conjugation without itself implying that the meaning began then.
rows.anchor: الفعل الحقيقي يدل على وجود معنى مصدره في الزمان بعد أن لم يكن في ماض أو حاضر، أو مستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qablu is built on ḍamm because it means an endpoint; detached from its genitive complement it becomes like part of a noun.
rows.anchor: وقبل: مبني على الضم، وإنما بني لأنه بمعنى الغاية

rows.speaker: الأخفش والزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash and al-Zajjaj say the answer to lammā is omitted, as in the verse about a Qurʾan moving mountains, with an implied “this Qurʾan would have been.”
rows.anchor: فجوابه محذوف، وهو لكان هذا القرآن عن الأخفش والزجاج

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says the long construction repeats itself and “they disbelieved” is the answer to lammā, comparing it with the repeated “that you will be brought forth” in 23:35.
rows.anchor: والجواب كفروا ومثل: (أيعدكم أنكم) إلى قوله: (أنكم مخرجون) عن المبرد

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says the first fa answers the first lammā and “they disbelieved” the second, paralleling 2:38.
rows.anchor: وهو قوله: (يأتينكم مني هدى فمن تبع هداي فلا خوف عليهم) الآية، عن الفراء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وأبي العالية وابن زيد والسدي
rows.claim: Qurayza and Nadir reportedly sought victory over Aws and Khazraj through Muhammad before his mission, then rejected him when he appeared among the Arabs; Muʿadh and Bashir reminded them of this, and Salam ibn Mishkam denied Muhammad matched their description.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية في ذلك، عن ابن عباس وقتادة وأبي العالية وابن زيد والسدي

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The phrase refutes determinists: God wants everyone to be godfearing and charges them so that they may attain taqwa.
rows.anchor: فيدل قوله: لعلكم تتقون على بطلان قول المجبرة في المخلوق والإرادة

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The victim would not necessarily die if not killed; otherwise retaliation would not preserve life, and killer and executioner would know death was inevitable anyway.
rows.anchor: لأنه لو كان إذا لم يقتل يموت لا محالة لم يكن في القصاص حياة

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Human acts originate with the human agent; if God created the killing, blame, liability to retaliation, and prohibition would be incoherent, refuting the determinists.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن فعل العبد حادث من جهته؛ إذ لو كان خلقه لما صح إيجابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes the obligation of retaliation.
rows.anchor: فأما الأحكام الشرعية: فتدل على وجوب القصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Retaliation may cover injuries as well as homicide: some injuries admit it, while others can spread to cause death.
rows.anchor: قد يتناول الجميع؛ لأن فيها ما فيه القصاص، وفيها ما لا قصاص فيه، ولكن لا يأمن أن يسري إلى النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Retaliation deters killers and preserves human life.
rows.anchor: في إيجاب القصاص زجرا للقاتل عن القتل، وفيه بقاء الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against the objection that parents, Muslims killing dhimmis, or free people killing enslaved people may escape retaliation, Jishumi says parental compassion prevents such killing and the others still fear a judge may impose retaliation.
rows.anchor: أما الوالد فما جبل عليه من الشفقة يمنعه من قتل ولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A group may be executed for one victim, since otherwise killers could enlist others to evade retaliation; Jishumi says there is no disagreement.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن الجماعة تقتل بالواحد؛ لأنه لو لم تقتل لم يؤمن أن من يهم بقتل واحد يستعين بغيره

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
rows.claim: If one person kills several, Abu Hanifa and his companions require execution without blood money.
rows.anchor: ولا دية عند أبي حنيفة وأصحابه

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi requires execution for one victim and blood money for the rest; if the heirs jointly choose execution, the blood money is divided among them.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي: تقتل بواحد ويغرم للباقي الدية. فإن اجتمعوا قتل، وتقسم الديات بينهم

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa takes “that” to refer to the preceding tamattuʿ and qirān, which he excludes for Meccans and those treated like them.
rows.anchor: ذلك يعني ما تقدم ذكره من التمتع والقران، عن أبي حنيفة ليس لأهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view permits Meccans to perform these rites without a sacrificial animal and takes “that” to refer to the animal.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لهم ذلك، وليس عليهم الهدي، وذلك إشارة إلى الهدي

words: مَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ أَهْلُهُ حَاضِرِي الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ
rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi identifies those exempt from the sacrifice as people whose home is beyond the Haram.
rows.anchor: عن الشافعي لمن لم يكن أهله حاضري المسجد الحرام وهو أن تكون داره وراء الحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Fear God” means avoid His sins and punishment.
rows.anchor: واتقوا الله يعني معاصيه وعقابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's severe punishment means His punishment is severe.
rows.anchor: يعني عقوبته شديدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse bars Meccans from the concession allowed to others, supporting Abu Hanifa's position.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على منع أهل مكة مما أبيح لغيرهم، وقد بينا الخلاف فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar is reported to hold the same rule; because it is not a matter of independent reasoning, Jishumi treats it as based on prophetic instruction.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عمر مثل ذلك، وذلك لا يعرف اجتهادا فحمل على التوقيف

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa counts residents within the miqats and onward to Mecca as residents of the Sacred Mosque.
rows.anchor: من كان في المواقيت وما بعدها إلى مكة

rows.speaker: مالك بن أنس
rows.claim: Malik ibn Anas identifies them as the people of Mecca.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك بن أنس: أهل مكة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi identifies them as people so close to Mecca that they cannot shorten the prayer on a journey there.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي: من كان بينه وبين مكة مسافة لا يقصر فيها الصلاة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to identify them as the people of the Haram.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنهم أهل الحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa's criterion is that those allowed to enter Mecca without iḥrām are like Meccans, unlike outsiders.
rows.anchor: واعتبر أبو حنيفة جواز دخول مكة بغير إحرام فهو كالمكي خلاف الآفاقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear God confirms that the preceding rites are obligatory.
rows.anchor: ويدل قوله: واتقوا الله على أن ما تقدم واجب؛ فلذلك أمر بإقامتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes the Murjiʾite claim that one who professes the two testimonies has nothing to fear.
rows.anchor: وتدل على بطلان قول المرجئة؛ لأن عندهم من أتى بالشهادتين، فلا خوف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To cover sins means to pardon them and not punish for them.
rows.anchor: أي يستر عليكم ذنوبكم بالعفو، فلا يعاقبكم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The min may be partitive or extra.
rows.anchor: قيل: (من) للتبعيض، وقيل: (من) زائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jishumi explains God's knowledge of deeds with the parallel that He knows what people conceal and disclose, as in 27:25.
rows.anchor: والله بما تعملون خبير أي عالم بأعمالكم ما تخفون وما تعلنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that a vow is an act of devotion.
rows.anchor: يدل قوله: أو نذرتم من نذر على أن النذر من القربات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A vowed act becomes binding like an obligation because it is paired with required spending.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن المنذور يلزم بمنزلة إلزامه تعالى من حيث قرنه بالإنفاق الواجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There will be no intercessor for wrongdoers in the afterlife, refuting the Murjiʾite doctrine of intercession.
rows.anchor: وتدل على ألا شفيع للظالمين في الآخرة، فيبطل قول المرجئة في الشفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense favors concealing all charity; scholars differ on the intended meaning, and Jishumi prefers Abu Ali's view as less open to suspicion and because most must be given to the imam.
rows.anchor: والأولى ما ذهب إليه أبو علي؛ لأنه أبعد من التهمة، ولأنه يجب دفع أكثره إلى الإمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakat is valid when given to a poor person, contrary to al-Shafiʿi's requirement to distribute among all eight classes.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن مصرف الصدقات الفقراء فوجب أنه إذا أعطى زكاته فقيرا جاز خلاف ما يقوله الشافعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expiation covers minor sins, not major sins, and therefore does not remove legal penalties or claims of blood.
rows.anchor: والمراد به الصغائر؛ لأنه لا يكفر الكبيرة؛ ولذلك لا تسقط الحدود والدم عن صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading establishes the duty to face the qibla; if instead the verse directs worshippers under uncertainty toward their considered direction, it validates ijtihad, and neither reading implies abrogation.
rows.anchor: التوجه عند الاشتباه إلى حيث يؤدي اجتهاده، فتدل على صحة الاجتهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the verse grants a choice of direction, it must have been abrogated when facing the Kaaba became obligatory.
rows.anchor: وإذا حملت على التخيير فلا بد من نسخ ذلك لوجوب التوجه إلى الكعبة

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAmir reads “they said” without waw; the other readers include it.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر: قالوا بغير واو، والباقون بالواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walad and ولد are two lexical forms rooted in birth.
rows.anchor: لغتان، وقد ذكرناه، وأصله من الولادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qunūt fundamentally means persistence and is used for obedience, prolonged standing, silence, and continuance.
rows.anchor: وأصل القنوت: الدوام، ثم يستعمل على أربعة أوجه: الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The obedience sense is illustrated by the command to Mary to be obedient to her Lord.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى: (يامريم اقنتي لربك)

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: When asked which prayer is best, the Prophet answered that it is the one with prolonged qunūt, illustrating long standing.
rows.anchor: وطول القيام كقوله، صلى الله عليه وسلم - لما سئل عن أي الصلاة أفضل، قال: طول القنوت

rows.speaker: زيد بن أرقم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Arqam said the Companions used to speak during prayer until the command to stand before God in qunūt was revealed, after which they stopped speaking.
rows.anchor: حتى نزل: (لله قانتين) فأمسكنا عن الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reportedly responds to Jews who called ʿUzayr God's son, Christians who called the Messiah His son, and Arab polytheists who called angels His daughters.
rows.anchor: نزلت في اليهود حين قالوا: عزير ابن الله، وفي النصارى حين قالوا: المسيح ابن الله، وفي مشركي العرب حين قالوا: الملائكة بنات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After refuting the Jews' argument about the qibla, the passage turns to their claim about God's unity.
rows.anchor: لما حكى الله تعالى قول اليهود في أمر القبلة ورد عليهم، ذكر قولهم في التوحيد ورد عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that God took a child is attributed to polytheists and others.
rows.anchor: يعني المشركين وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subḥānah declares God exalted above taking a child.
rows.anchor: سبحانه يعني تنزه عن اتخاذ الولد

words: بَل لَّهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All that is in the heavens and earth belongs to God by creation and ownership; Jesus and others are created, owned, and governed, and the Creator cannot have a child because that would make Him a body.
rows.anchor: بل له ما في السماوات والأرض ملكا وخلقا، فنبه بذلك على أن المسيح وغيره خلق له، مملوك مربوب

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن عباس
rows.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Abbas gloss “all are qunūt to Him” as “obedient.”
rows.anchor: قيل: مطيعون، عن مجاهد وابن عباس

words: فَمَنْ عُفِيَ لَهُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ شَيْءٌ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة والربيع والأصم وأبو علي وأبو القاسم وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: The first view says the killer is spared execution by the victim's heir in return for blood money; “his brother” refers to the killer and “something” to the retaliation right.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قول ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة والربيع والأصم وأبي علي وأبي القاسم وأبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most jurists and Abu Ali say compensation is established by mutual agreement; others say it is owed without agreement, depending on what intentional homicide makes obligatory.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم: يثبت المال بتراضيهما، وهو مذهب الأكثر واختيار أبي علي، ومنهم من قال: يثبت بغير تراض

rows.speaker: الأكثر
rows.claim: The majority say blood money comes from the killer's property, which Jishumi says is the jurists' consensus.
rows.anchor: فقيل: من مال القاتل، عن الأكثر، وعليه إجماع الفقهاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan are reported to place the blood money on the killer's clan, the ʿāqila.
rows.anchor: وقيل: على العاقلة، عن ابن عباس والحسن

rows.speaker: علي بن موسى القمي
rows.claim: A second view makes the blood heir the person pardoned: after accepting compensation by agreement, he should collect it graciously from the killer; Ismail ibn Ishaq also transmits this from Malik.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن موسى القمي، وذكره إسماعيل بن إسحاق عن مالك

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: A third view says the blood heir pardons by giving the killer the remainder owed alongside retaliation.
rows.anchor: الثالث: فمن عفا له ولي الدم بأن دفع إليه بقية ما يجب مع القود، عن السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third view works only with a report permitting reciprocal payment alongside retaliation for sex or free-status differences, which Jishumi says is invalid.
rows.anchor: وقد بينا أن ذلك لا يصح، فعلى هذين العفو بمعنى الإعطاء

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi prefers the first view: pardon ordinarily means remission, here waiving retaliation, and most exegetes support it.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي: الأول؛ لأن الظاهر من العفو هو السقوط والترك، وهو ترك القود، ولأن أكثر المفسرين عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jishumi asks why the verse says “something” from the brother when retaliation cannot be divided; the excerpt ends before his answer.
rows.anchor: ومتى قيل: كيف قال: من أخيه والقود لا يتبعض، وما الفائدة فيه؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One comparison makes the qibla favor like the favor of the message, since God does what is most beneficial.
rows.anchor: أن النعمة في أمر القبلة كالنعمة بالرسالة؛ لأنه تعالى يفعل الأصلح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another comparison says commanded remembrance is like the prophetic mission in the greatness of its station, and devotion magnifies blessings.
rows.anchor: أن الذكر المأمور به كالنعمة بالرسالة فيما ينبغي أن يكون عليه من المنزلة في العظم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ allows kamā to answer the command to remember God, alongside “I will remember you”; remembrance is required so God will remember them with mercy and prior favor.
rows.anchor: نعم عند الفراء، وجعل ل اذكروني جوابين: أحدهما: كما، والثاني: أذكركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā in kamā may be a verbal-noun particle meaning “like our sending,” or a particle that makes the construction indeclinable.
rows.anchor: قلنا: (ما) المصدر، كأنه قيل: كإرسالنا فيكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recalling the blessings of qibla and guidance, the passage turns to the Messenger as one of the greatest blessings.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر تعالى إتمام نعمه بالقبلة والهداية عقبه بذكر الرسول؛ إذ هو من أعظم النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger is Muhammad, Arab by lineage; his Arab identity honored them, encouraged them to follow him, and made his message accessible to their understanding.
rows.anchor: يعني محمدا - صلى الله عليه وسلم - منكم نسبا؛ لأنه من العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs recited may mean God's proofs or the Qurʾan with its commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: قيل: الحجج، وقيل: القرآن وما فيه من الأوامر والزواجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One gloss says the Messenger calls people to practices that purify them if followed; another says he praises them by describing them.
rows.anchor: قيل: يدعوكم إلى ما إذا تمسكتم به صرتم أزكياء، وقيل: يزكيكم بالثناء والمدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb may mean purifying, or, per Abu Muslim, God increasing the people, uniting their hearts, and bringing them toward growth.
rows.anchor: قيل: يطهركم، وقيل: يكثركم الله به ويؤلف بين قلوبكم ويقربكم من الزكاة التي هي النماء، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view calls the Book the Qurʾan and distinguishes the terms: signs are proofs, the Book is written text, and wisdom is religious teaching and practices, so the wording is not redundant.
rows.anchor: الآية: الحجة، والكتاب: المكتوب، والحكمة: ما فيه من إعلام الدين وشعائره فليس بتكرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading attaches “recites” to the Messenger's delivery, while “teaches the Book” means teaching its meanings and contents.
rows.anchor: والمراد به الأداء (ويعلمكم الكتاب) معاني الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the Book as the Qurʾan and wisdom as the Prophetic Sunnah and rulings known only through him.
rows.anchor: والحكمة السنة وما لا يعلم إلا من جهته من الأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view says he recites principles of divine unity and justice not in a Book, teaches the laws, and teaches accounts of earlier peoples unknown to the Arabs.
rows.anchor: يتلو ما ليس فيه كتاب من أصول التوحيد والعدل ويعلمكم الكتاب أي الشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final phrase may mean that God taught the Arabs scripture and knowledge they lacked, laws, accounts of earlier peoples, or all these.
rows.anchor: لم يكن لهم كتاب ولا علم فعلمهم ذلك، وذلك من أعظم النعم

rows.speaker: المشبهة
rows.claim: The anthropomorphists cite the verse to claim God may literally come.
rows.anchor: استدلت المشبهة بالآية على جواز المجيء على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jishumi rejects literal coming as a bodily property: a coming body would resemble bodies and undergo change through motion or rest, contrary to 42:11.
rows.anchor: وقد قال تعالى: (ليس كمثله شيء)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since a command is an accident and cannot itself come, the phrase means its place or those subject to it; rational and transmitted evidence rule out literal coming, and figurative usage is common.
rows.anchor: المراد محل الأمر، ومحتمل الأمر، ولا يقال: إنه توسع ومجاز من وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coming is most likely in the afterlife, because “the matter is decided” fits the afterlife.
rows.anchor: الأقرب أن المراد به في الآخرة؛ ولذلك قال: وقضي الأمر وهذا لا يليق إلا بالآخرة

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm says God comes to them with what He promised and threatened, refuting those who allow Him to break His threat.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أنه تعالى يأتيهم بما وعد وأوعد، عن الأصم، فيبطل قول من يجوز الخلف في الوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of revival is said to occur only in a prophet's time, since it functions as a miracle.
rows.anchor: ولا شبهة أن مثل هذا لا يقع إلا في زمان نبي؛ لأنه يجري مجرى المعجزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqātala is the reciprocal form of killing; qatlu with fatḥa means killing, with kasra the enemy, and a person's maqātil are vulnerable points where a wound is fatal.
rows.anchor: المقاتلة: مفاعلة من القتل، والقتل بفتح القاف مصدر قتله قتلا، وبكسر القاف العدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted line uses iqtitāl to mean fighting.
rows.anchor: واعتراني من عامر بن لؤي ... في بلاد كثيرة الاقتتال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fight follows people whose flight did not save them, encouraging believers and warning them against fleeing.
rows.anchor: لما أراد الله تعالى حثهم على الجهاد قدم ذكر أولئك الذين فروا فلم ينفعهم الفرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may be to the Companions, urging jihad and preventing them from following those who fled.
rows.anchor: خطاب للضحابة حثا على الجهاد ومنعا من سلوك أولئك في الفرار

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak takes the command as addressed to those just mentioned: they were ordered to fight, fled, were killed and revived, then ordered to fight again.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك: أمروا بالجهاد ففروا، فأماتهم، ثم أحياهم، ثم أمرهم بالجهاد

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali explains God's path as His religion and the way He prescribed for its vindication.
rows.anchor: يعني في دين الله. وطريقه التي شرع لهم لإعزازه، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations take God's path to mean obedience to Him or fighting the enemies of believers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: في طاعته، وقيل: في جهاد أعداء المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears what hypocrites say and knows what they love, so believers should beware of Him.
rows.anchor: واعلموا أن الله سميع لما يقوله المنافق عليم بما يحبه، فاحذروا حاله
